caption: Pixel: every seventh pixel in the count lit - the dots fall into diagonals because each row carries the count on
why: Most coordinates are measured, 0..1, so a pattern stretches to fit any size. Sometimes you want to count instead: every third LED, the fifth column, a pixel at a time. Pixel gives each pixel's whole-number column, row and index.

`index` counts the pixels the way the picture is laid out, row by row, so a pattern built on it runs along the rows like a strip. Its neighbours: Coords measures 0..1, so a pattern scales with the panel; Pixel counts, so a pattern keeps its spacing in LEDs.
steps: Pixel has no inputs or settings. `x` is the column (0 .. width-1), `y` the row, and `index` is row times width plus column.
`index` plus a clock (**Time** times 20, added) goes into a **Modulo** with m 7: a number that runs 0..7 and starts again every seven pixels, and creeps along twenty pixels a second.
A **Smoothstep** with edges 1 and 0 turns that into 1 where the remainder is near 0, fading by 1: one bright pixel in every seven. That is the **Palette**'s brightness.

The matrix is 32 wide, not a multiple of 7, so each row starts at a different point in the count: the dots line up in diagonals. That is the index carrying on from the end of one row to the start of the next.
`y` times 1/16 picks the colour, so each row has its own.

try.label: Every eighth
try.text: the Modulo's m at 8: 32 is a multiple of 8, so every row starts at the same point in the count and the dots stack into straight columns.

try.label: Faster
try.text: the clock's Multiply at 80: the dots race along the rows four times as fast.

try.label: Sparse
try.text: the Modulo's m at 32: one pixel in each row of 32 - a single dot running along every row, each row a step behind the last.
